cervical-radiculopathy: Cervical Radiculopathy pinched nerve in neck arm pain from neck cervical disc nerve root Neck & head Nerve problems Neck and arm pain, usually arm pain more troublesome than neck pain. Pins and needles, numbness or weakness in a root-specific pattern. Worse with neck extension and turning to the painful side; may ease with hand on head. Atypical features that point elsewhere: both arms or legs involved, clumsy hands, gait change, bladder change, constant night pain unrelated to position. cervical-myelopathy: Cervical Myelopathy spinal cord compression neck clumsy hands DCM degenerative cervical myelopathy Neck & head Nerve problems Clumsy or numb hands (trouble with buttons, writing, dropping things). Unsteady, stiff or wide-based walking; feeling that the legs are heavy. Symptoms in both hands or both legs, though one side may be worse. Neck stiffness; electric-shock feeling down the spine on neck flexion (Lhermitte sign). Later features: bladder urgency or incontinence, bowel change. Neck pain may be mild or absent. Do not rely on pain. Tandem walk (heel to toe) and Romberg test (standing with feet together, then eyes closed). Hand function: grip, finger movement, grip-and-release test. Full neurological screen: dermatomes, myotomes, reflexes in all four limbs.
cervicogenic-headache: Cervicogenic Headache headache from the neck neck headache occipital headache Neck & head Neck & back pain Usually one-sided headache, starting at the back of the neck or head and spreading forward. Brought on or worsened by neck movement or sustained neck postures. Reduced neck movement, often rotation. Neck stiffness or ache with the headache. Not typically throbbing with nausea and light sensitivity (these point more toward migraine), though overlap can occur. whiplash-associated-disorder: Whiplash-Associated Disorders (WAD) whiplash neck injury car accident neck WAD whiplash associated disorder Neck & head Neck & back pain Neck pain and stiffness beginning within hours to a day after the crash. Headache, often occipital. Shoulder girdle and upper back pain. Dizziness, poor concentration, fatigue, sleep disturbance, anxiety about driving. Arm pain or tingling suggests grade III. Neurological examination of the upper limbs.

Pain and stiffness with sustained postures (desk work, phone use, driving) and end-range movement. Limited range of movement, often rotation and side flexion. No neurological signs; no red flags. rib-related-pain: Rib-related Pain: Rib Dysfunction, Costochondritis and Rib Fracture rib pain costochondritis rib fracture rib dysfunction chest wall pain rib related pain Back, chest wall & pelvis Ligament, joint & cartilage injury Sharp, localised chest wall pain reproduced by pressing on a specific spot. thoracic-serious-pathology: Thoracic Serious Pathology and Visceral Referred Pain visceral referred pain thoracic red flags chest pain referred to back thoracic serious pathology Back, chest wall & pelvis Neck & back pain Pain not changed by movement, posture or rest. Height measurement compared with previous records.

Neurological examination is often normal in neurogenic TOS; wasting of hand muscles is uncommon but serious. May spread to the buttock or thigh but not with a clear nerve-root pattern. No progressive weakness, no saddle numbness, no bladder or bowel change. Pain often changes day to day and is influenced by activity, sleep and stress. Symptoms are often less bothersome when cycling or when walking uphill because the spine is more flexed. No clear stiffness of passive movement, unlike frozen shoulder. Acute tear picture: sudden pain and weakness after a fall or heavy lift, especially in a younger person or in someone who cannot lift the arm. This needs early medical opinion (see G). The end of range feels firm and painful, not just painful. Usually older than 50 to 60 or a history of earlier shoulder injury.
